tool.name: NAVEdge
tool.summary: NAV-Edge, normalised anisotropy variance (Zhang, Ravat, Marangoni & Hu 2014, Geophysics 79(3), J43-J53): a normalised, Gaussian-weighted variance in a moving window, with the Gaussian stretched along strike. Positive over sources and negative outside them, so the edges are the zero crossings.
tool.usage:
Best applied to a magnetic grid that has been reduced to the pole (RTP) or the equator (RTE). Also works on gravity grids.

Uses no higher derivatives, so it is less sensitive to noise than derivative-based edge detectors: use a window of 3 for clean data and larger windows for noisy data.

The local strike is taken from Gaussian-derivative filters and rounded to 10 degrees.

param.name: in_raster
param.dialogReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).
param.pythonReference: Grid to process (a single-band raster; no-data cells are left as no-data in the result).

param.name: out_raster
param.dialogReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.
param.pythonReference: Output raster (GeoTIFF), with the input's extent, cell size and coordinate system.

param.name: window_size
param.dialogReference: Window size M in pixels (odd). The Gaussian's standard deviation is (M - 1) / 6.
param.pythonReference: Window size M in pixels (odd). The Gaussian's standard deviation is (M - 1) / 6.

param.name: anisotropy_scale
param.dialogReference: Anisotropy scale (cof): 1 is isotropic; larger values smooth along strike and sharpen across it, separating close parallel sources (the paper uses 1, 2 and 5).
param.pythonReference: Anisotropy scale (cof): 1 is isotropic; larger values smooth along strike and sharpen across it, separating close parallel sources (the paper uses 1, 2 and 5).
